mainTopic: Bones and sinews of the פסח, רב's rule on sinews, and why נותר is not burned on יום טוב
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation. Bones of ordinary קדשים found in piles, some opened, need no burning, but bones of the פסח may still hold marrow because of the איסור of שבירת העצם. רב then rules that all sinews count as meat except the neck sinews. The גמרא challenges him from our משנה: the 'sinews' burned on the sixteenth seem to be neck sinews, and burning them implies they are meat. Three אמוראים defend רב by rereading the משנה. רב חסדא says it means the גיד הנשה according to רבי יהודה, רב אשי says the fat of the גיד הנשה, and רבינא says the outer sinew described by שמואל. Next the גמרא asks why נותר is not burned on יום טוב itself, since an עשה overrides a לא תעשה. חזקיה, אביי and רבא each bring a different פסוק to answer, and רבא's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Bones of ordinary offerings found in piles need no burning
steps.stepSummary: Bones of ordinary קדשים found in piles, some with their marrow removed, do not need burning. We assume the owner removed and ate the marrow from all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he found them in piles, and some of them had their marrow removed. Bones of קדשים, where the איסור of breaking a bone does not apply: he removed the marrow from all of them and ate it, and they do not need burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to the question of how bones of קדשים differ from bones of the פסח. It describes the exact case: bones found in piles, some already emptied of marrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ordinary קדשים there is no איסור of שבירת העצם, so the owner was free to crack every bone open. Since some are clearly opened, we assume he opened all of them in time and ate the marrow. Nothing is left that would count as נותר, so no burning is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking a bone, which is forbidden with the קרבן פסח
Burning, the required way to dispose of נותר

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'שמצאן צבורין צבורין' are the tail of an answer that began earlier on the דף, describing the case being discussed.

phrases.english: that he found them in piles,
phrases.notes: Continuation of an answer begun on the previous amud

phrases.english: and some of them had their marrow removed.
Bones of offerings
to which the prohibition of breaking a bone does not apply —
he removed the marrow from all of them
and ate it,
and they do not need burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an answer on the previous amud explaining the difference between bones of קדשים and bones of the פסח
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case definition: the difference shows up when bones are found in piles with some opened
steps.terutzMaskana: Ordinary קדשים bones: we assume all were opened and eaten, so no burning

steps.title: Bones of the פסח may still contain marrow
steps.stepSummary: With the פסח, breaking bones is forbidden, so we cannot assume all were opened. Some may still contain marrow and need burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bones of the פסח, where the איסור of breaking a bone does apply: perhaps he removed the marrow from these, but from those he did not, and they need burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by contrasting the פסח with ordinary קדשים. Here we cannot assume every bone was emptied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the איסור of שבירת העצם stopped the owner from freely cracking the bones, finding some opened tells us nothing about the rest. The unopened ones may still hold marrow that became נותר, so they need checking and possibly burning.

keyTerms.meaning: The bones of the קרבן פסח

steps.whatToRemember: The איסור of שבירת העצם is the reason for the difference. With ordinary קדשים we assume all bones were opened. With the פסח we cannot, so leftover marrow may need burning.

phrases.english: Bones of the Paschal lamb
to which the prohibition of breaking a bone does apply —
perhaps these are the ones he emptied,
and those he did not empty,
and they need burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַצְמוֹת הַפֶּסַח דְּיֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם שְׁבִירַת הָעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on the איסור of שבירת העצם
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח bones cannot be assumed emptied, so they may need burning

steps.title: All sinews count as meat except the neck sinews
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, rules that all sinews are considered meat, except the sinews of the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: all the sinews are meat, except the sinews of the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a rule from רב about whether sinews count as meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling sinews 'meat' means they are treated as part of the edible קרבן, so one can eat them as the פסח. The neck sinews are too hard to count as food and are left out.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
All the sinews are meat,
except for the sinews of the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: sinews, which are the next item listed in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All sinews have the status of meat except the neck sinews

steps.title: Citing the משנה about burning sinews
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה: bones, sinews and נותר are burned on the sixteenth. This sets up a challenge to רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: the bones, the sinews and the נותר are burned on the sixteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה to set up a challenge to רב's rule. The analysis comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists sinews separately from נותר as something that must be burned. The גמרא will ask which sinews these must be.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover sacrificial meat past its time

phrases.english: We learned: The bones, the sinews, and the leftover
shall be burned on the sixteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that will be used to challenge רב's rule
steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that neck sinews are not meat
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing sinews among the things burned on the sixteenth
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that neck sinews are not meat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires burning 'sinews' listed separately from נותר. The גמרא will show these must be neck sinews, and burning implies they are meat.

steps.title: Which sinews does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of sinews the משנה is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: These sinews, what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kind of sinews the משנה requires burning. This sets up the elimination that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not just a request for information. By asking it, the גמרא can rule out the options until only the neck sinews remain.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: These sinews — what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind the משנה just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which sinews the משנה says must be burned

steps.title: Ruling out regular sinews and leftover sinews
steps.stepSummary: The משנה cannot mean regular meat sinews, since those should be eaten. It also cannot mean leftover sinews, since those are already included in נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means sinews of meat, let us eat them! And if it means ones that were left over, that is the same as נותר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the two possible readings of 'sinews' in the משנה, one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sinews count as meat, they should be eaten, not burned. If they are meat sinews that simply went uneaten, they are already covered by the word נותר, so listing them separately would be pointless.

phrases.english: If we say sinews of meat —
let us eat them!
And if ones that were left over —
that is the same as leftover!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Eliminates possible answers to the question in step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both readings of 'sinews' as ordinary meat sinews
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Edible sinews should be eaten, and uneaten ones are already included in נותר

steps.title: The משנה must mean neck sinews
steps.stepSummary: Since the other options fail, the משנה must mean neck sinews. This sets up a challenge to רב, who said neck sinews are not meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious: sinews of the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the משנה is talking about neck sinews. This prepares the challenge against רב in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary sinews are either eaten or already included in נותר, so the separately listed 'sinews' must be the neck sinews. But the משנה requires them to be burned, which suggests they are treated as meat. That is the opposite of רב's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'sinews' that the משנה says must be burned separately seem to be the neck sinews. Since burning implies they are meat, this challenges רב's rule that neck sinews are not meat.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious: sinews of the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both other options are ruled out, the only remaining reading is neck sinews, which sets up the challenge to רב
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה seems to refer to neck sinews, which sets up a challenge to רב's rule that they are not considered meat

steps.title: If neck sinews are not meat, why burn them? A challenge to רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its challenge to רב. The משנה burns neck sinews, which makes sense only if they are meat. According to רב they are not meat, so why burn them?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say they are meat: that is why they need burning. But if you say they are not meat, why do they need burning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge to רב. If neck sinews are not meat, as רב says, there is no reason for the משנה to require burning them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only leftover meat of a קרבן (נותר) has to be burned. Something that is not meat at all could simply be thrown away. Since the משנה burns neck sinews, it seems they are meat, which contradicts רב.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say they are meat,
because of that they need burning.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לָאו בָּשָׂר נִינְהוּ —
phrases.english: But if you say they are not meat —
why do they need burning?
phrases.notes: They could just be thrown away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 7 (the משנה means neck sinews) to challenge רב's ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that neck sinews are not meat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only meat (נותר) needs burning. The משנה burns neck sinews, so they must be meat, contradicting רב.

steps.title: The משנה means גיד הנשה according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the sinews in the משנה are the גיד הנשה, following רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The משנה is only needed for the גיד הנשה, and according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives a new way to read the משנה: the 'sinews' are the גיד הנשה, not neck sinews. He ties this to רבי יהודה, whose view the גמרא will quote next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This defends רב. The משנה's 'sinews' are not neck sinews at all, so the משנה says nothing against רב's rule. The burning is explained by a special case involving the גיד הנשה, which needs רבי יהודה's view to make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is needed only for the sciatic nerve,
and according to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 by giving a different reading of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's sinews were neck sinews, and burning them implied they are meat, contradicting רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's sinews are the גיד הנשה, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is defending רב. By showing the משנה's sinews are the גיד הנשה rather than neck sinews, he removes the challenge to רב's rule.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only one גיד הנשה is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: the prohibition of גיד הנשה applies to only one thigh, and logic points to the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יהודה says, it applies only to one, and logic decides it is the right one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב חסדא's answer. רבי יהודה holds that only one of the two nerves is forbidden by the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since logic says the right one but there is no clear proof, both nerves are removed from the קרבן. Both cannot be eaten, so both are burned, which explains the burning in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
It applies only to one,
phrases.notes: Only one thigh's nerve is forbidden.

phrases.english: and logic decides it is the right one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רב חסדא's reference to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's reading that the משנה is about גיד הנשה according to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה that only one גיד הנשה is forbidden, likely the right one.

steps.title: Attempt to prove רבי יהודה was unsure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the burning that רבי יהודה was in doubt about which nerve is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, resolve that רבי יהודה was in doubt. For if it were clear to him, the permitted one we should eat and the forbidden one we should throw away. Why burn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle an open question: was רבי יהודה sure it is the right nerve, or only guessing? It says the burning shows he was unsure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה knew for certain, the left nerve would simply be eaten and the right one thrown away. Burning both only makes sense if we cannot tell which is which. So it seems רבי יהודה must have been in doubt.

phrases.english: But then, resolve
that Rabbi Yehuda was in doubt.
For if it were clear to him,
the permitted one we should eat,
and the forbidden one we should throw away —
why does he need burning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב חסדא's answer to draw a new conclusion about רבי יהודה's certainty.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה was unsure which nerve is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's requirement to burn, as explained by רב חסדא.

steps.title: The nerves were known, then mixed up
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא בר חיננא rejects the proof: the case is where they knew which nerve was which, but later the two got mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא בר חיננא said: For example, where they were known, and in the end they were mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב איקא בר חיננא shows the proof does not work. Even if רבי יהודה was sure, the משנה can be about a case where the nerves got mixed up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first everyone knew which nerve was forbidden and which was permitted. Then they got mixed together, so no one can tell them apart, and both must be burned. The burning comes from the mix-up, not from doubt in רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: For example / such as a case where

phrases.english: Rav Ika bar Chinnana said:
For example, where they were known,
and in the end they were mixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attempted proof of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof that רבי יהודה was in doubt; רב חסדא's reading stays in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The burning can come from a later mix-up, so it does not show that רבי יהודה himself was unsure.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's burning of sinews can be explained as the גיד הנשה according to רבי יהודה. This does not prove רבי יהודה was unsure which nerve is forbidden, because the case may be one where the nerves were known and then got mixed.

steps.title: רב אשי: the משנה means the fat of the sciatic nerve
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers a different answer to the question of Step 8: the 'sinews' that must be burned are really the fat of the גיד הנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The ruling of the משנה is needed only for the fat of the גיד הנשה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second answer to the earlier question 'sinews are not meat, so why burn them?'. He says the משנה is talking about the fat around the גיד הנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא needed רבי יהודה's opinion to explain the משנה. רב אשי finds a case that works for everyone: the fat of the גיד הנשה. As the next step shows, this fat is Torah-permitted, so it counts as real meat that becomes נותר, yet nobody eats it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (the ruling refers only to a specific case)
the sciatic nerve, forbidden by the Torah

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is needed only
phrases.notes: The burning in the משנה refers only to this case.

phrases.english: for the fat of the sciatic nerve.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the קשיא of Step 8, parallel to רב חסדא's answer in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the 'sinews' are the fat of the גיד הנשה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sinews are not meat, so there should be no reason to burn them as נותר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fat of the גיד הנשה is Torah-permitted meat that is left uneaten, so it is burned as נותר.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the fat is permitted, but Jews treat it as forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב אשי: the fat of the גיד הנשה is permitted, but the holy Jewish people keep away from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Its fat is permitted, but the Jewish people are holy and treat it as forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show why the fat of the גיד הנשה fits the משנה's rule about burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the Torah permits the fat, it has the status of real meat and cannot just be thrown away. Since the Jewish people have a custom not to eat it, it stays uneaten past the deadline. That makes it נותר, which must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
the Jewish people are holy (they take on extra strictness)
they treat it as forbidden (a custom)

steps.confusionAlert: The fat is NOT forbidden by the Torah. It is permitted by law and avoided only by custom. That is exactly why it counts as meat that must be burned.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Its fat is permitted,
but the Jewish people are holy
and treat it as forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind רב אשי's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the fat of the גיד הנשה is meat that ends up burned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the fat is permitted, but the Jewish people treat it as forbidden.

steps.title: רבינא: the משנה means the outer sinew
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a third answer: the משנה is talking about the outer sinew, following רב יהודה in the name of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The משנה refers to the outer sinew, in line with what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives yet another answer to the Step 8 question. He says the sinew to be burned is the outer one, and he points to a teaching that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's answer depends on there being two sinews with different levels of prohibition. He sets this up here, and the next step quotes שמואל's teaching to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: regarding the outer one (the outer sinew)
and in line with what רב יהודה said

phrases.english: Ravina said: It refers to the outer one,
and it is like what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative answer to the קשיא of Step 8, after רב חסדא and רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the outer sinew.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sinews are not meat, so they should not need burning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The outer sinew is permitted by the Torah, so it has the status of meat and becomes נותר.

steps.title: שמואל: two sinews, inner Torah-forbidden and outer not punished
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: there are two sinews. The inner one is forbidden with lashes. The outer one is forbidden but carries no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: There are two sinews. The inner one, next to the bone, is forbidden, and one is liable for eating it. The outer one, next to the meat, is forbidden, but one is not liable for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שמואל's teaching, which explains רבינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outer sinew is forbidden only by the רבנן, so by Torah law it is permitted meat. Because nobody eats it, it is left over and becomes נותר, which needs burning. This explains why the משנה says sinews are burned.

keyTerms.meaning: one is liable (to lashes) for it
that is next to the bone

steps.confusionAlert: Both sinews are called 'forbidden' (אסור). The difference is the level: the inner one is a Torah prohibition (with lashes), and the outer one is only rabbinic (no lashes).
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers to 'why burn sinews?': רב חסדא says the גיד הנשה according to רבי יהודה, רב אשי says the fat of the גיד, and רבינא says the outer sinew. All three point to something that is Torah-permitted 'meat' that ends up uneaten.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
There are two sinews:
the inner one, next to the bone,
is forbidden, and one is liable for it.
phrases.notes: A Torah prohibition, punished with lashes.

phrases.english: The outer one, next to the meat,
is forbidden, but one is not liable for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the teaching רבינא relied on.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's claim that the outer sinew is burned as נותר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל: the outer sinew is forbidden without lashes, meaning it is only rabbinic.

steps.title: Why not burn the leftovers on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the 16th falls on שבת, burn on the 17th. It asks why the burning is not done on יום טוב itself, since an עשה overrides a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If the sixteenth falls on שבת, etc.' Why? Let the positive מצוה (to burn) come and push aside the prohibition (of doing work on יום טוב)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה and challenges it. Why wait for a later day when the burning could be done on יום טוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that a positive מצוה‎ (עשה) overrides a negative prohibition (לא תעשה). Burning נותר is an עשה, and doing work on יום טוב is a לא תעשה. So the מצוה of burning should win, and the leftovers should be burned on the 15th.

keyTerms.meaning: etc. (the rest of the quote from the משנה)
a positive מצוה overrides a negative prohibition

phrases.english: 'If the sixteenth falls (on שבת)' etc.
And why? Let the positive מצוה come
and push aside the prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? נֵיתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְיִדְחֵי לֹא תַּעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the leftovers are not burned on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The general rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה should allow burning on יום טוב.

steps.title: חזקיה: the Torah gives a second morning for the burning
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה, and the school of חזקיה, explain from the extra words 'עד בקר' that the burning belongs on the second morning, not on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said, and the school of חזקיה taught the same: The פסוק says, 'Do not leave any of it until morning, and what is left of it until morning you shall burn in fire.' The Torah did not need to say 'until morning' a second time. So why does it say 'until morning'? To give it a second morning for its burning.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question by reading the פסוק closely. The repeated words 'עד בקר' tell us that the burning happens on the next morning, not on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of עשה overriding לא תעשה does not apply here, because the Torah itself scheduled the burning for a 'second morning', the 16th. The מצוה of burning simply does not start on יום טוב. When the 16th is שבת, it is pushed off to the 17th.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse did not need to say

steps.whatToRemember: The burning of נותר is set by the Torah for the 'second morning' (the 16th). So it never overrides יום טוב, and if the 16th is שבת it waits until the 17th.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: a מצוה does not override a prohibition at a time when the Torah never set the מצוה to apply.

steps.title: אביי: Only שבת's own offerings belong on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers from the verse 'עלת שבת בשבתו': only שבת's own burnt-offering is done on שבת. A weekday offering is not done on שבת or on יום טוב, so burning leftovers, which is not that day's מצוה, waits.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The verse says, 'The burnt-offering of שבת on its שבת.' This means the burnt-offering of שבת is done on שבת. But a weekday burnt-offering is not done on שבת, and a weekday burnt-offering is not done on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer to the question of why the leftover meat is not burned on יום טוב itself. He uses a different verse than חזקיה did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בשבתו' (on ITS שבת) teach that a holy day only allows the offerings that belong to that day. Burning נותר is not a מצוה that belongs to the holy day, so it counts like a 'weekday' act and cannot be done on שבת or on יום טוב. Because of this, the rule that an עשה overrides a לא תעשה never gets started here.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The burnt-offering of שבת on its שבת' (במדבר כח:י)
A weekday offering, meaning something that does not belong to the holy day
'The verse says', which introduces a proof from a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The verse only says 'שבת,' but אביי reads it as covering יום טוב too. That is why the extra line 'and not a weekday offering on יום טוב' appears.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since an עשה overrides a לא תעשה, the burning should be done on יום טוב itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בשבתו' teaches that acts which do not belong to the day, such as burning leftovers, are not done on שבת or on יום טוב.

steps.title: רבא: On יום טוב, only food itself may be prepared
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a third answer from 'הוא לבדו יעשה לכם.' The word 'הוא' excludes acts that only prepare for the food (מכשירין). He then begins to explain 'לבדו,' and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse says, 'Only that may be done for you.' The word 'that' teaches: that itself, but not the things that prepare for it. The word 'only'...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another answer to the same question. He uses the verse about which kinds of work are allowed on יום טוב, and the step continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Work on יום טוב is allowed only for food (אוכל נפש). 'הוא' narrows this further, so even acts that only make the food possible are not allowed. Burning leftover meat is not food preparation at all, so it surely is not allowed. 'לבדו' adds a second limitation, which the גמרא explains next.
